summary: He opposed voting for Trump throughout the 2024 cycle and told his audience to stay home. He says his negative view began around 2023, and he was against Trump by election day. His warning was that Trump would take the country to war with Iran, would not carry out mass deportations, and had handed the movement to donors, Silicon Valley and, in his framing, Jewish interests. In early 2025 he gave the administration a conditional "fair shake," blamed donors and the people around Trump rather than Trump himself, and praised specific actions (tariffs, parts of the national security strategy), while saying his loyalty is to America First, not to Trump. Through 2025 and into the 2026 Iran war his criticism hardened: he says "personnel is policy" and Trump chose the wrong people; that the second term serves Israel, Jewish donors and Trump's own interests; that the administration covered up the Epstein files; that Trump does not care about white Americans; that Trump himself, not his advisors, is "the problem"; and that Trump failed to wield the executive power he had. By September 2026 his opposition is total: he says MAGA "has died" and Trump "is acting as the enemy." He still judges individual actions on their merits, and his verdict on Trump's whole arc since 2015 is that it did real good ("on net Trump is good," Jan 2026; "it's not to say that his entire legacy is bad," Sep 2026). Neither softens his opposition. He wants something new and more radical, not Vance or Rubio.

timeline.period: Before the transcripts (~2023–2024, as he recounts it)
timeline.note: His negative outlook on Trump predates the transcripts; he dates it to around 2023, when he says he warned that "they're working to install Trump" for a war with Iran (recollection, Apr 2025). Throughout the 2024 cycle he told his audience not to vote for Trump ("don't vote, don't vote. This is a Jewish nightmare," recollection, Feb 2026). He floated conditions for his vote, a commitment against war with Iran (Aug 2024, as he recalls it) and mass deportations, that Trump did not meet. By election day he was against Trump, and he says he did not vote at all. He cites the Adelson donation, the Vance pick, the disavowal of Project 2025 and pro-legal-immigration promises. These are his later recollections; the corpus begins Nov 19 2024.

Post-election: says the cabinet picks (Rubio, Bessent, Lutnick, Bondi and others) confirm his warning of "gays and Jews in the cabinet" (Nov 22), and predicts mass deportations are not "a serious promise." Dated post-election commentary: he agrees with Jared Taylor that it is "preferable that Trump won" (Nov 20). Says Trump "has good instincts, but he is constrained by government" (Nov 25) and feels "some sense of relief" that Trump will not go to jail. Calls the incoming government "the most pro-israel administration ever" and says a president should "prosecute his enemies" (Dec 3).

Inauguration: dated post-election commentary, not his 2024 stance. He says he "didn't really want him to win… I was a little conflicted" and is "relieved to see him win," but did not vote and "couldn't support him politically" (Jan 20). Says he will "give him a fair shake." Lists positives (executive orders, personnel) and concerns (Iran, deportation numbers, H-1B, a cabinet "not aligned," since "personnel is policy"). By Feb 17 he says failure on mass deportations would be "a serious betrayal." Through Jan–Feb he blames the tech billionaires and donors rather than Trump ("in his heart of hearts, Trump is more aligned with us," Jan 27) and says Musk has put Trump "in the backseat" (Feb 11). Says Trump "restored the legitimacy of the government" (Feb 5). Calls the influencer Epstein binders a "publicity stunt" (Feb 27).

Criticizes the campus antisemitism crackdown and Iran policy as serving Israel. Praises specific actions: calls the tariffs "the best thing he's done" (Apr 7); says he would "commend Trump" if Trump withheld military aid from Israel over Gaza (May 12); sets a "victory condition" on deportations and the wall that would make him "eat my hat" (Jun 10). June: US strikes Iran, which he calls vindication of his 2024 warning. Admits he was wrong about the JFK files: "They did release the files" (Mar 21). Says "it's a valid argument that Trump is still a net positive," and that the movement "must give way to a more radical movement" (Apr 16). Says "I trust Trump. I don't trust any of these other people" and urges him to "go full Caesar" (May 27). On the 10th anniversary of the campaign launch, says Trump "became everything that he swore to destroy," while judging that on net he "might have been a positive" (Jun 16). After the June strikes he says Trump "was goaded" into them.

The DOJ "no client list" memo (Jul 7): calls it "the Jeffrey Epstein cover-up by the Trump administration." After the Iran strikes, amnesty talk and the memo, he burns his MAGA hat and urges others to (Jul 8). Argues Trump, Vance and the GOP work for billionaire and "Jewish Zionist" donors. Nov: says Trump tried to "bury and cover up" the files until Congress passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act. Dec 2025: loyalty "comes with a price tag"; still praises the national security strategy as "a very solid document" (Dec 5). Calls the budget bill "an unequivocal landmark historic victory for Trump" (Jul 3). Says Trump is "most likely in the files" (Jul 18), was "involved in some way" and lied about it (Sep 8), and that he doubts Trump himself committed a sex crime (Sep 9). Says Trump "does not care about the white man" (Aug 21). Credits the West Bank annexation statement (Sep 25), deterrence toward Venezuela (Oct 10) and the ICE raids in Chicago while refusing to vote "for more of this" (Oct 2). Says "2025 is the year that MAGA died" (Nov 14) and calls Trump "the first white race hustler" (Dec 1).

Credits the Minneapolis enforcement push as "one thing that is good" while calling Trump "super corrupt" (Jan 27). Epstein is "an albatross"; he is "barely rooting for Trump anymore" (Feb 11). Iran war begins (Feb 28): "I told you so." Says "Trump is the problem," not his personnel, and that Trump chose AFPI over Project 2025 (Mar 16–19). Says Trump crowns Levin and Loomer as MAGA (Mar 16). Calls Trump "evil" after the Easter post (Apr 6); announces he will vote Democrat in the 2026 midterms (Apr 8; see midterms). Jan 15: rejecting calls to throw out Trump's legacy, he gives a whole-arc verdict on the movement since 2015, "on net Trump is good" (defeating political correctness, changing the immigration debate), and says the job is to "take the baton and carry it forward."

"Israel controls this party" (May 19). Calls the June ceasefire a move against "Israel's interest" and mocks the pro-Israel backlash (Jun 16). Says Trump was "elected to do this" by Jewish oligarchs, Adelson and AIPAC, and that Massie lost because Trump intervened (Jun 8). Argues the second term is about Trump protecting and enriching himself, via "his Jewish fixers" (Jul 1); says Trumpism is "tapped" and "in 24, Trump had to be defeated" (Jul 13); says the government suppresses the dissident right (Aug 4). Aug 24: "if he did what he said he would it would have been great," and, as later commentary, "Are you starting to see now why I wanted Kamala?" Says Trump "could have done it. He blew it again" on wielding executive power (May 7). Calls Trump "a complete and total failure" (Aug 24).

After Trump's UN speech on Iran: "MAGA has died," Trump "is acting as the enemy" ("it's not to say that his entire legacy is bad"), and "something radically different" is needed (Sep 22). Lists Epstein cover-ups and the war among the ways the second term "blew it," and tells his audience to stay demoralized so they are not taken in again in 2028 (Sep 24). Says Trump widens presidential power without using it, handing a stronger office to the next Democrat (Sep 9), and that "Trump is the one that shut down the Epstein files" (Sep 14).

Backs the FBI raid on Ilhan Omar's home in principle ("I fully support this here") but calls it "far too little too late," predicts the administration will back down, and says it should have drawn up an enemies list of thousands on day one; after Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation calls the administration "a criminal enterprise" (Oct 13).

summary: He describes Vance as a political creation of Peter Thiel and the Silicon Valley "PayPal mafia": Thiel, he says, gave Vance a "series of no show jobs," funded his Senate race and, with Musk and Tucker Carlson, got him picked as VP. He says Vance's populism is a rebrand of a neocon-mentored Never-Trumper who voted for McMullen, praised Obama and (citing a Vanity Fair profile he read on air) advised the Clinton campaign. He says Vance serves Silicon Valley, Wall Street and "Zionist tech patrons," is "in the pocket of Israel" behind deniable wording, and failed to stop the 2026 Iran war when he alone could not be fired. He says the donor class and "the Jewish money" are shifting to Rubio, leaving Vance to own the war. He argues Vance won't be strong on immigration or white nativism, citing his race-blind populism and his non-white family. He says a Thiel-funded network of online influencers promotes Vance. He opposes Vance for 2028 ("Never Vance 28"); the conditions he names (an immigration moratorium, restraining Israel, distance from Thiel and Musk) are demands he says Vance has not met. By August 2026 he expects him to be the nominee but predicts he will fail without Trump's cover.

timeline.note: Cites Vance's selection as VP, which he says Musk, Thiel and Tucker Carlson lobbied for, as evidence that MAGA had been taken over by Silicon Valley and a reason not to vote for Trump.

Post-election: predicts "they're gonna try and get you behind vance in 2028" (Nov 21). Dec 3 segment on the Vances' Thanksgiving photo argues Vance's marriage shows he is not the white-identitarian figure some claimed.

Jan 23: says the 2028 succession cannot go to Vance and the goal is to bring down or counter the Thiel-backed national populism. Jan 31 and Feb 14: lays out the Thiel/Frum backstory and the "series of no show jobs," and dismisses the Munich speech as marketing aimed at the base.

Mar 24: floats, as "pure speculation," that the leaked Yemen Signal chat was meant "to make Vance look good." Apr 22: "So I won't be voting for JD Vance in 2028. I don't trust him." Jun 2: "JD Vance is a creation of Peter Thiel" and the influencers "shilling for Vance" are paid by Thiel. Jun 5, during the Trump–Musk split: if Vance and Musk are conspiring against Trump, "I ride for Trump all day." Jun 21, the night of the US strikes on Iran: calls the report that Vance pushed back "a planted story."

"Fuck Vance" in the same segment where he burns his MAGA hat (Jul 8). Aug 2025 (after Tucker Carlson criticized him): details the Thiel, Frum, Mithril "no-show job", Rockbridge/1789 Capital and Tucker ties. Aug 19: segment on Vance's wife and children.

Sep 1: says Vance had "some no-show job at Peter Thiel's venture capital firm" and the GOP cannot transfer Trump's following to him. Oct 30, after Vance's Turning Point USA event: "you can have the Israel first money or you can have the America first votes, but you can't have them both," and the votes are "conditional." Nov 11: pro-Vance influencers are "on the payroll"; Vance will be "the same or worse" than Trump.

Responds to Vance's "can eat shit" remark and TPUSA speech: says Vance is trying to have it both ways, and sets conditions (immigration, restraining Israel, his relationship with Thiel and Musk) for any support.

Feb 5: "Trump is Vance's tomb." Feb 5: responds after Vance condemns him in an interview. Iran war: "Never Vance 28" (Feb 28). Says the Wall Street donors and "the Jewish money" have moved to Rubio, who distances himself from the war, and that reports of Vance as the anti-war negotiator are planted to save his 2028 prospects (Mar 23–27). Says Vance did not dissent (Apr 8).

Describes a "shadow war" between Vance and Rubio (May 7). Says Vance is "in the pocket of Israel" (Jun 8). Treats Tucker Carlson as a Vance operative (see tucker). After the Rogan interview (Jul 16) says Vance "breadcrumbs" Israel critics while keeping pro-Israel donors, as the donors line up behind Rubio. Aug 5: calls the Tucker/Vance program a race-blind class populism meant to deflate white nativism. Jun 18: on Vance's press conference about Israel, "a position is being implied" but not taken. Aug 6: "2028, I'm not voting Rubio. I'm not voting Vance. I'm voting for an alternative."

Aug 31: "Vance is the nominee. I think that might be unavoidable." positions.statement: He opposes Vance as Trump's successor ("Never Vance 28") and has since January 2025 ("it cannot be Vance"). He rejects the idea that the 2028 nomination has already been decided. The conditions he names are demands Vance has not met: an immigration moratorium, restraining Israel and distance from Thiel and Musk; "until we get an answer on that… you don't have my support and you'll never get it" (Dec 2025). In October 2025 he warned Vance against condemning the groypers, saying neutrality might keep them out of it and doing "something for America first" might earn their votes. Since the Iran war began he says he will not vote for the administration figures who took the country to war, and in August 2026 said he is "voting for an alternative." His remark that Vance's nomination "might be unavoidable" (August 2026) is a prediction, not a change of stance; his hope is that Vance fails (see vance-12).

summary: He has had a running feud with Tucker Carlson that he says began in 2022, when he helped defeat Carlson's friend Joe Kent and Carlson, he says, worked with Max Blumenthal on a piece calling him a fed. Throughout the transcripts he argues Carlson comes from a CIA family and is himself an intelligence-connected operative rather than a journalist. He calls Carlson a gatekeeper and limited hangout on Israel and the Jews: late to the issue, still pro-Israel, insisting it is not about Jews ('blood guilt'), and drawing a line to exclude him. He also calls Carlson's folksy populist persona a recent rebrand by a rich, intelligence-connected establishment figure. The feud peaked in August 2025, when Carlson and Candace Owens called him part of a campaign to discredit anti-neocon voices and a 'weird gay kid' in a basement. After a thaw that began in September 2025 and an interview with Carlson in October 2025, he praised Carlson's courage and defended him against the Israel lobby, but within weeks he said Carlson was using the interview to paint him as an antisemite, and by December 2025 he called it part of a Vance-aligned effort to neutralize his following. He repeated that in May 2026, after Carlson said he regretted the interview. In 2026 he credits Carlson's opposition to the Iran war but treats him as a Vance operative, dismisses his break with the GOP as a pose for Vance 2028, and attacks his race-blind, economics-first 'populism', his closeness to Gulf states and Muslims, and his left–right alliance.

timeline.period: Before the transcripts (as he recounts it)
timeline.note: Neutral to supportive of Carlson in 2017–19; critical in 2020 when Carlson did not back Stop the Steal; the beef begins in 2022, when he helped defeat Joe Kent and a Grayzone piece by Max Blumenthal's wife, which he ties to Carlson, called him a fed.

Mocks Carlson's persona and says he is CIA-connected: a 'fed' and 'spy' after the Qatar trip (Mar 11 2025). Apr 10: answers Carlson's insinuation (on Alex Jones) that he is a fed: 'Tucker Carlson is a CIA agent.' May: says Carlson took 25 years to criticize Israel and still supports it. Earlier items: says Carlson, 'whose dad ran Voice of America' and who 'applied for the CIA', helped elect Javier Milei in Argentina (Nov 26 2024). Ties Carlson to Vance's venture firm (Feb 14 2025). Says Carlson privately called Trump 'a demon' around January 6 (Mar 25). Calls Carlson, Dave Smith and Tim Pool the approved 'reasonable voices' (Apr 10).

Calls the Ted Cruz interview 'phenomenal' but an ambush by a propagandist (Jun 18); argues Carlson opposes an Iran war as a CIA 'prioritizer' focused on China. The Iran president interview adds to his view that Carlson is an intelligence asset (Jul 7). Says Carlson admits Israel runs a blackmail ring yet still supports Israel (Jul 15). Says Carlson 'fashioned himself only recently' as a populist (Jun 18). 'Tucker's not one of us. Tucker's one of them'; 'It cannot be Vance. Can't be Tucker' (Jul 16).

He says that on Carlson's show, Carlson and Candace Owens called him part of a campaign to discredit anti-neocon voices, a fed, and a 'weird gay kid' in his parents' basement. He answers with a three-hour rebuttal (Aug 1: Joe Kent history, Carlson's father and the CIA, Vance ties, 'I am a spokesman for the disaffected white man') and a part two on Buchanan and Buckley (Aug 8). Challenges Carlson to have him on: 'Interrogate me like you interrogated Ted Cruz' (Aug 1).

After Charlie Kirk's assassination the tone softens: 'maybe me and Tucker are in something like a detente', and in the same segment calls Carlson's Kirk comments pandering (Sep 19); he groups himself with Carlson as the honest ones against Levin and Hammer (Oct 8). He says Carlson phoned him after the August rebuttal; Carlson's interview with him airs in late October. He credits Carlson's courage (Oct 28), defends him during the Heritage Foundation backlash and says they are on the same team against the Israel lobby despite disagreements (Oct 29 – Nov 17). Earlier, he expected Carlson and Owens, 'far more outspoken' on Israel than Kirk, to fill the space Kirk left (Sep 16), and said Israel's 'most wanted man is Tucker' (Oct 8). Raises Carlson's CIA family again on Oct 22; rebuts Josh Hammer's claim that the feud was staged ('That was real', Oct 29). Nov 4: 'I think he is America first. I think one day he'll be fully with us.'

The relationship sours: Carlson 'brings me on the show to teach me not to be anti-Semitic' (Nov 19) and never mentions the interview without calling him an antisemite (Dec 1); 'that guy's an operative' (Dec 4); 'No one shills JD Vance more than Tucker Carlson' (Dec 23). Credits the Huckabee interview but rejects its Ashkenazi argument (Feb 23). Calls the interview and Carlson's Piers Morgan appearance a 'JD Vance hive mind effort' and 'the one, two punch' of a playbook against his following (Dec 1, Dec 26). Attacks the 'blood guilt' line in Carlson's AmericaFest speech (Dec 23). Rejects Carlson's left–right alliance (Jan 14–30). Feb 3: 'I don't know what Tucker is.'

Iran war: credits Carlson as the one voice discouraging it and says he stands with anti-war figures (Mar 2–9), but doubts Carlson's account of CIA interest in his texts to Iran and sees him building Vance's peacemaker image (Mar 17–27). May 4: Carlson tells the NYT he regrets the interview and says race is a distraction from economics; he says the interview was meant to neutralize him. Defends Carlson against Patrick Casey's 'smuggling Islam' charge and says 'Tucker is doing a good job… I know he hates me' (Mar 9). 'Tucker will never say it's Trump' (Mar 17). 'Tucker is breaking… Better late than never', but objects to Carlson's defense of Islam (Apr 6).

Calls Carlson's exit from the GOP a pose to bring voters back for Vance (Jun 23); answers Carlson's 'fake like Nick Fuentes' remark (Jun 25); 'Tucker is the bulldog for JD Vance and Palantir' (Jul 1). Attacks the Aug 5 ten-point plan as race-blind 'sloppulism' and a runway for Vance. In Sep says Vance took the 'blood guilt' line from Carlson and attacks Carlson's promotion of Abdul El-Sayed (Sep 1–3). Mentions become sparse after Sep 16.

After Buckley Carlson attacks him on X, he answers the fed accusation by listing the Carlson family's ties to the CIA, Palantir and Vance's office, and says Carlson is grooming commentators to support Vance in 2028 (Oct 14).

positions.statement: He calls Carlson a gatekeeper and limited hangout on Israel and the Jews. passages.title: What colorblind meritocracy means
passages.text: And so in his mind, the answer to immigration, which is anti-white, the answer to affirmative is color blind meritocracy. Well, that's interesting. The answer to anti-white policies is not a pro-white politics. The answer to anti-white policies is not to examine where that's coming from. The answer to an explicitly and a majority anti-white system is color blind meritocracy. And what is that supposed to mean? It's supposed to mean that if there are disparities in the country, we're going to accept them if the disparities result from a meritocratic system that is fair. And so that means that, for example, in Harvard, if you get all Chinese students, We're not going to look at the fact that they're all Chinese, we're going to consider whether they were the most qualified applicants at the admissions office. And as the country is importing these high-skilled people, Indians, Chinese, and so on, instead of getting DEI, where they artificially are selecting blacks and Hispanics who underperform, The top Chinese and Indians from a population of a billion people that are imported into the country. That's a colorblind meritocracy. And it's like, so wait a second, you know, that sounds good on paper. Obviously, that's- better in some respects than DEI where we're elevating incompetent people, but is it really better if we're trading places instead of rewarding underperforming native minorities? We're rewarding overperforming imported foreigners. But according to colorblind meritocracy, that is something that would be fine.

passages.title: The conceit of Tuckerism

They realized that white people are rightly furious and the expropriation of our resources and property. White people are losing our country through immigration, through socialist redistribution. There's this cultural imperialism happening. White people are losing everything everywhere. And Trumpism was an expression of this. Build the wall, kick the people out, kick the bastards out. … and the conceit of Vance, the conceit of Tucker Carlson, the conceit of Joe Kent, of all these people with their pluralistic race blind populism. As I really believe they are trying to deflate any kind of white nativist feelings. … And I think that these Republican CIA types, they basically see this as an existential threat to America. that America is going to be ripped apart by this racialized politics, that the race war will come first in the form of tribalized politics. summary: He calls on right-wing voters to punish the Republican Party in the November 2026 midterms by not voting Republican. In 2025 his call was to stay home; since the Iran war began in February 2026 he says he himself is voting Democrat, and he tells followers that staying home or voting Democrat both serve the purpose. He says Republicans broke their promises (no mass deportations, no border wall), took the country to war with Iran for Israel and buried the Epstein files, and so deserve a historic defeat. He wants a Democratic House, and ideally a Democratic Senate, so that Democrats use their oversight powers to investigate, subpoena and impeach Trump and his cabinet. He says voting Democrat is purely a tactic to punish and pressure the GOP: he is not a Democrat, calls the Democrats worse, and would not back one for president in 2028. He exempts a few America First Republicans such as Thomas Massie. His stated aim is to weaken the GOP, which he calls Israel-controlled and impossible to reform from inside, so that a more radical right-wing outsider can take it over in 2028 or 2032. He argues the base should withhold its vote the way donors and the Israel lobby withhold money. He has predicted since January 2025 that the midterms would force the administration to drop mass deportations, and that Republicans would lose the House, and by September 2026 predicts a blue wave of about 50 seats and a Democratic Senate.

timeline.note: Predicts early that Trump will probably lose the House in 2026 and that midterm politics will stall mass deportations (Jan 21 2025). Recalls having told his audience not to vote Republican in 2018, the 2021 Georgia runoff and 2022 (recollection, Mar 11 2025). Jan 20 2025: 'In the midterms, there must be accountability. We have to primary them in two years time'; predicts Trump 'will lose the house'.

Predicts midterm politics will make mass deportations 'politically untenable' (Feb 4) and that Democrats will win the House and subpoena power. Says 'You can't start mass deportations during the midterms… We did it in 2018' (May 23). Calls his vote conditional on what Republicans deliver.

Says he is 'just out' rather than voting for the left (Jul 8). Makes his vote conditional: without mass deportations 'we will not vote in the midterms' (Jul 3). After the Epstein 'no client list' statement: 'Forget the midterms' (Jul 8); says the 2026 midterms need to be 'a Democrat avalanche' and 'an historic loss' (Jul 16). Calls his vote 'a bargaining chip' (Aug 19) and warns 'we will fucking throw it for you' (Aug 20); answers the argument that Democrats would be worse by saying things get worse every year under both ('How could it get any worse?').

Nov 3: 'one day you're gonna wake up in the Groyper party.' Nov 13: 'We won't be there in 26 and we'll be there in 28' (in the GOP primary). After the Virginia and New Jersey elections predicts Republicans will be 'slaughtered' (Nov 11). During the fallout from his Tucker Carlson interview, says America First voters will show up in 2026 for candidates like Thomas Massie and against any politician who disavows Tucker (Nov 17).

Says the administration is backing off mass deportations because of the midterms, as he predicted (Jan 16–27). Feb 16: 'Do not vote in the midterms. The Republicans have to lose'; hopes a Democratic House impeaches Trump. Feb 5: 'my message is in 2026, stay home.' Feb 18: 'if we get a war with Iran, forget it. I'm not voting in 26.'

The Iran war begins Feb 28; on Mar 2 he says 'I'm gonna hold my nose and vote for a Democrat', and on Mar 4 calls his own past non-voting a mistake. Wants Democrats to win both chambers for oversight (Mar 5), says the Democratic vote is for the midterms only (Mar 11), wants Trump impeached but not removed so that Vance does not become president (Mar 16). Apr 8: 'I'm voting for the Democrats in 2026'; in 2028 he will vote in the Republican primary for an America First candidate or sit out.

In Ohio he urges a vote against Vivek Ramaswamy for governor, for the Democrat if need be (Dec 2025 – May 2026). After Massie loses his primary (May 19), says the GOP cannot be taken over from inside and he will encourage his followers to vote Democrat 'out of pure vengeance' (May 19). Lays out the strategy: weaken the GOP, then a 'hostile takeover' by a dark-horse outsider in 2028 or 2032 (May 27, Jun 8). Names exceptions to 'get them all out': Thomas Massie and James Fishback (Apr 27); welcomes Ken Paxton's Texas primary win (May 26). May 5: staying home is an option, but 'if you really want to make a difference' vote Democrat.

Calls for 'a blue wave' and Trump's impeachment (Jun 30); rejects a left–right alliance and says the GOP is the vehicle to take over (Jul 8); calls a GOP loss over Iran a 'pain mechanism' (Jul 15). Says the blue wave is 'already over' (Aug 18) and argues for divided government (Aug 27). Says Trump's corruption, measured by his personal profits, is 'actually worse than it is with the Democrats' (Jul 1). Wants Democrats in 'to hurt Vance a little bit' (Aug 17).

Reads Trump's UN remark that he does not care about the midterm results as confirmation (Sep 22). Cites the GOP donor Tim Mellon's boycott: the base should 'stay home in 26' unless Republicans deliver (Sep 23). On new polls (32% approval, Democrats +8 on the generic ballot) predicts Republicans lose about 50 House seats and the Senate, and warns his audience not to be won back for Vance in 2028 (Sep 24). Sep 14: his America First Foundation scorecard gives no member of Congress better than a C+. Sep 29: 'this is why I tell the young white men, don't vote Republican.'

The constant is 'don't vote Republican' (September 2026).

summary: He argues that mass immigration is the existential threat to America and Europe: in his framing, white people are being "replaced" and "outbred" by non-white foreigners, a process he calls "white genocide," and he wants the United States to be majority white. He wants as much of this reversed as possible (a wall, a moratorium, deportations) while acknowledging the demographic math: from March 2026 he says a white majority is "not coming back," that the chance to reverse it has passed, and that the aim now is to "regain control over our empire" and "ameliorate the worst effects of diversity." He says the objection is to the country becoming non-white itself; he cites crime, costs and failed assimilation too, but as secondary. He calls for an immigration moratorium that ends legal as well as illegal immigration, and treats "high-skilled" H-1B and student-visa migration from India and China as no better than illegal immigration. He wants a permanent border wall and all illegal immigrants deported (10 to 20 million, by visible enforcement at job sites and, if necessary, by locking down cities), an end to birthright citizenship, and denaturalization of naturalized citizens he sees as hostile. He holds that being American is a matter of ancestry, not paperwork. He blames the business and donor class and both parties for immigration, and calls open borders "Jewish policies." Trump's failure on deportations is covered under trump.

timeline.period: Before the transcripts (as he recounts it)
timeline.note: Says that in June 2024 he refused to vote for Trump unless Trump committed to removing everybody and to an immigration moratorium (recollection, Feb 2026). Predates the transcripts.

Post-election: says the incoming administration is promising 'more legal immigrants' and no mass deportations, though it may secure the border. Dec 3: against the 'colorblind meritocracy' of skilled Indian and Chinese immigration ('America's not for them'). Dec 11: names mass immigration 'making the country less white' as a main priority to reverse. Nov 20: unless Trump deports "10 million people or even like 5 million," the country is worse off.

H-1B fight: says skilled and unskilled immigration have 'functionally the same' result, that 'the population is being replaced,' and that immigration 'benefits capital.' Jan 20–21: backs ending birthright citizenship and says a wall matters because executive enforcement can be undone. Feb 20: mass deportation means "sweeping neighborhoods." Mar 4: the original aim was "zero or negative on immigration." Apr 3: "we don't want any more non-white people coming here."

Backs job-site raids (Jun 6). After the Supreme Court injunction ruling, calls birthright citizenship 'the biggest problem with illegal immigration' (Jun 27). On the Big Beautiful Bill, says a million removals a year 'would be huge' but opposes the farm-worker amnesty (Jul 3). May 23: a million removals a year is "the minimum to me to qualify for mass deportations." Jun 26: immigrants should not hold office until they have been here "a generation at least." Jul 16: "We wanted the deportations before. Now it's bigger than that. You had your chance."

Against Joe Kent and Tucker Carlson: "No matter how much merit these people have, we want America to remain coherent, racially" (Aug 1). Says America is "now a multiracial empire" that must be "governed like an empire" (Aug 26). Welcomes the $100,000 H-1B fee (Sep 19), then: "We want the H one B program to be scrapped" (Sep 23).

After the white-refugee policy, says, in a light register, 'We can bring in some white people if they have the right politics' (Oct 15). 'We want the country to be majority white' (Nov 5). Welcomes Trump's 'permanent pause' on third-world migration if it becomes policy (Dec 1). Dec 17–23: repeats the moratorium demand; tells Vivek Ramaswamy he is at most a guest. Oct 30: lists housing costs and wages among the harms. Nov 10: "Blood and soil, for me, open borders for thee." Dec 2: "what country do we still need immigrants from?"; says he would get "back on board" with Trump only for results, such as a million illegals deported in a year, not for rhetoric.

Minneapolis/ICE: calls mass migration 'the engine of white genocide' and open borders 'Jewish policies' (Jan 26); calls for denaturalizing Somali fraudsters. Jan 27: "30 million deportations" is "what winning looks like." Feb 17: Republicans "won't raid job sites because their donors employ the illegals."

After the Minneapolis drawdown and reports that the White House was dropping mass deportations: "you can't just stop the water from pouring in, you have to bail out the water," and that "the immigration issue is over," Trump "blew it," and the aim now is "to regain control over our empire" (Mar 11). "We are closer to establishing a lunar colony than we are to even having a majority white nation ever again… It doesn't mean give up on that. It doesn't mean I'm not in favor of white identity politics" (Mar 30).

Calls for a wall and a moratorium under a strong executive (May 7). Jun 29: 'It would be easy to deport all of them'; blames the business community and a 'uniparty.' Jun 30: birthright ruling ('a horrible system'). Jul 30: mass migration is snuffing out the West; says Jews, as an 'eternal minority,' push immigration (see jewish-power). May 1: "We're already a non-white country." May 4: people would accept a recession for "some semblance of a white country again." Jun 9: "It doesn't need to be an all white country. I know that's not coming back"; says "liberal Jews" bring the immigrants in. Jun 29–30: ending birthright by executive order is "hopeless." Jul 27: "we're gonna have to re-migrate all these people."

Says he has backed a moratorium "ever since Charlottesville" (Aug 18). Faults the administration for "not building a border wall" (Aug 4). After the birth-tourism order: "You're never stopping immigration. You're never reversing any of this" (Aug 7).

UT Austin crowd: the problem is that America 'is becoming majority non-white,' not crime or jobs (Sep 22). After Trump's UN speech, calls immigration 'the real existential threat,' not Iran, and says every illegal alien not deported under Trump has effectively been amnestied (see trump). Sep 14: on the UT Austin crowd, "We have to begin to think about a legal justification to get rid of them." Sep 22: on Hispanic polling, the deportation opportunity was "once in a lifetime" and "we just blew it."

On Dinesh D'Souza, says even a fully assimilated immigrant 'does not identify as an American' and that long-resident immigrants 'have got to go back' (Oct 5); says the promised deportation operation 'has been abandoned' (Oct 6).

positions.statement: He argues that mass immigration is the existential threat of our time: in his framing, white Americans and Europeans are being replaced and outbred by non-white foreigners in a "white genocide," which he calls "a deliberate program," and once outnumbered they will be "outvoted in a democracy." He wants America to be a white, "European-descended nation," with countries "just for Europeans," and said in November 2025 "we want the country to be majority white." He calls the invasion "the real existential threat" (September 2026); his view that a white majority is not coming back, and what follows from it, is immigration-11.

summary: He supports high, permanent tariffs as the core of a nationalist economic program to rebuild American industry, and called Trump's April 2025 "Liberation Day" tariffs "the best thing he's done." He counts tariffs among the three pillars of the Trump program, with mass deportations and no new wars. He wants them set in a comprehensive tariff schedule alongside industrial policy (subsidies, research, intellectual-property protection). He backs tariffs as leverage too (he praised the 2019 tariff threat that made Mexico hold asylum seekers), but wants them to stay in place as permanent policy rather than be lifted once concessions are won. He opposes the free-trade and supply-side consensus, which he says sent factories abroad, enriched a rival China and served asset-owning elites. He judges the administration's trade record a failure: it backed down within a week, the tariffs were sloppy and were struck down and refunded, and by 2026 he said there were "still no tariffs"; he says the botched execution has turned the public against tariffs, not that the policy was wrong. He describes the wider economic record (frozen job market, inflation, war costs, giveaways) as serving donors rather than Americans. He also argues the country is "bankrupt" and in "stagflation," which from 2026 he ties to the Iran war. He says the core issue is not the economy but the nation, and that he would accept left-wing economics in exchange for closed borders.

timeline.note: Counts destroying 'the free trade consensus' among Trumpism's achievements (Nov 21). Praises Trump's threatened 25% tariff on Canada and Mexico as leverage on the border: 'That's the wonder of tariffs' (Nov 25).

Hopes for "across the board tariffs on all imports" (Jan 20). Backs "a 25% across the board tariff on imports" and supports the Canada and Mexico tariffs "as a tool of statecraft," but says "we need them to remain" as permanent policy rather than be lifted once concessions are won (Jan 31).

Wants 'tariff man' and a directed industrial policy, 'not corporate tax cuts and austerity' (Feb 18). Blames trade policy (NAFTA) for sending factories abroad (Feb 26). Mar 24: says Trump is walking back his protectionist agenda and using tariffs only as a foreign-policy tool; calls for high, targeted, permanent tariffs as 'a nationalist economic program.'

Liberation Day: 'This is the best thing he's done'; tariffs are 'designed for American workers,' and the outcry comes from elites and oligarchs (Apr 7). Apr 10: after the pause, 'He totally capitulated and we lost the tariff regime.' Apr 2: "It might be the best policy, economic policy in like a century." Apr 7: "tariffs are not a tax on consumers." Apr 9: the goal "has shifted from reshoring manufacturing to decoupling from China."

After the court ruling: 'I like the tariffs' but they were 'sloppy' (May 28). Jul 15: 'He backed down on all the tariffs. He backed down on China.' May 23: credits Biden's industrial-policy laws as "stepping the right direction." Jun 13–19: "country's bankrupt," largely "because of trade." Jul 3: against ending the clean-energy credits. Jul 31: objects to new tariffs on Canada over Palestine, "on behalf of Israel."

"If Trump were serious, we could have tariffs and subsidies and we could make stuff" (Aug 20). "We're about to enter stagflation" (Sep 4). "The country is bankrupt. The country is insolvent" (Sep 19).

Says free trade with China enriched a strategic rival and a trade war with China is easy to justify (Oct 23). Lists tariffs among his top three reasons for backing Trump (Nov 5). Proposes a left–right bargain: the right gives up 'free market' and 'free trade' economics, the left gives up mass migration (Nov 19). Dec 17: the tariffs are 'not bringing back manufacturing.' Dec 17: says the promises that tariffs would pay down the debt or fund a dividend were lies; "we are in stagflation territory."

Supreme Court strikes down the emergency tariffs. He still calls himself 'a tariff supporter' (Feb 18) and says Trump's instincts are protectionist and "the ideas are sound," but that the botched execution has people saying "tariffs are horrible" (Feb 24–25). May 7: 'there's still no tariffs'; calls for a tariff schedule. Feb 24: calls the ruling "an unforced error by Trump." Mar 19: "the winning formula is reindustrializing America with protection and tariffs." Apr 1: the Iran war's energy shock is "catastrophic for the United States."

Rejects Tucker Carlson-style economic framing: 'it's not about the economy' (Jul 30). Mocks Trump's $5,000 promise (Sep 9) and says Trump's UN speech shows he does not care about Americans' costs and purchasing power (Sep 22). Jul 15: "We got Reaganomics." Jul 24: "It's not the economy, stupid." Aug 10: ending the Iran war is "an economic necessity." Aug 24: "completely dependent on China." Sep 14: Trump "could have explored national security tariffs."

positions.statement: He supports high tariffs, and from January 2025 backed "a 25% across the board tariff on imports." He called Trump's April 2025 "Liberation Day" tariffs "the best thing he's done" and "the best policy, economic policy in like a century." He argues that tariffs are designed for American workers and industry rather than elites and multinationals, that "tariffs are not a tax on consumers," and that the short-term pain and inflation are worth it. He was still calling himself "a tariff supporter" in 2026.

positions.statement: He wants tariffs to be permanent, predictable and across the board, set in a tariff schedule and combined with industrial policy (subsidies, tax credits, research and development, intellectual-property protection), in "a nationalist economic program" to rebuild productive capacity. He also values tariffs as leverage: in November 2024 he praised Trump's 2019 tariff threat that made Mexico hold asylum seekers ("That's the wonder of tariffs"), and in January 2025 he said of the Canada and Mexico tariffs "I support it as a tool of statecraft, but we need them to remain." His objection is to tariffs used only as short-term bargaining chips and then lifted. He credits Biden's industrial-policy laws as "stepping the right direction" (May 2025) and opposed ending the clean-energy tax credits because "the United States needs to electrify" (July 2025).

summary: He opposes US wars in the Middle East, which he argues are fought for Israel rather than for America. He says Iran poses no strategic threat to the US, that Israel drew the US into the June 2025 strikes and the 2026 war, and that Israel sabotages every US–Iran deal, so the answer is for Washington to restrain Israel. During the 2026 war he said openly that he was rooting for Iran as a counterweight to Israel, and by mid-2026 he says the US suffered a strategic defeat. He calls Israel's Gaza campaign a genocide and ethnic cleansing and says US support for it destroys American credibility. Citing a 2026 report, he says Netanyahu knew of October 7 in advance and let it happen. He is not a blanket non-interventionist: he wants Ukraine conceded to Russia's sphere and aid cut, and says he has become less pro-Russia since mid-2025; from October 2025 he backs 'hemispheric defense' interventions in the Americas (Venezuela, Greenland, Cuba). He argues the US is overextended and needs 'a managed retreat'. He treats China as the long-run great-power rival, but since the Iran war says the US must first free itself from 'world Jewry', which may be the bigger threat.

timeline.note: Calls Israel's conduct in Gaza war crimes and a genocide, and says the double standard against Russia is costing the US its credibility. Says Ukraine should be conceded to Russia ('Give them the land'). After Assad falls (Dec 11), says Israel needs Trump for 'the last thing', regime change in Iran. Contrasts "$26 billion for Israel" with an unbuilt border wall, and says October 7 "was never just about Gaza" but about Iran (Dec 11).

Recalls that his 2024 rallying cry was 'no war with Iran' (Jan 20). Blames Trump's first-term pressure on Venezuela for the migrant wave (Jan 20). Calls China the main rival in 'a new cold war' (Jan 28, Feb 18). Ukraine: says Russia is winning and the aid is 'bankrupting the United States' (Feb 28). Says an Iran war would be 'the next worst thing' after Iraq (Mar 5) and that Israel wants US strikes to trap the US in a regional war (Apr 16). Says Israel is sabotaging the US–Iran talks (Apr–May).

Israel strikes Iran and the US joins on Jun 21: 'This is not our war.' He blames Israel and its 'American Jewish allies' for drawing the US in and predicts a second round. Before the strikes, says Netanyahu 'stood down on October 7th' (Jun 11). Frames the choice as restraining Israel or being drawn in (Jun 19).

On Ukraine says he is 'no longer as pro-Russia' and the US is 'kind of winning' (Jul 15). Calls Gaza 'a genocide and an ethnic cleansing' (Aug 5) and says his popularity comes from opposing it. After the Alaska summit, says the US should cut aid to Ukraine and 'Let Russia have Ukraine' on China-first grounds (Aug 15). Calls the Venezuela boat strikes a 'new war' on a false pretext (Sep 4–5), then from Oct 10 backs US action in the hemisphere under the Monroe Doctrine. Says the US needs 'a managed retreat' (Oct 22). Says he used to think being pro-Russia was 'based and edgy' (Dec 5).
Backs the Venezuela operation and Greenland under the Monroe Doctrine ('hemispheric defense') while opposing any Iran war (Jan 12–15). Says Israel 'cannot tolerate a deal' with Iran (Feb 17).

The 2026 Iran war begins (Feb 28). Says 'Israel is the problem' and Washington must restrain it (Mar 2). Says he is 'rooting for Iran to win this strategic victory' (Mar 12). Argues world Jewry, not China, may be the biggest threat (Mar 27). Calls the war 'a war of choice' (Mar 12) and says the US has 'effectively lost' (Mar 30).
At the April 7 ceasefire: 'We just surrendered.' Says 'There is no winning scenario here' (May 12).

Under the MOU and after it: 'Iran won, Israel lost' (Jun 17); 'a humiliating strategic defeat' (Jun 15); 'We lost' (Aug 7). Says Israel will sabotage any deal (Aug 10). Says 'I really hope that we invade Cuba' (Jun 16).

Citing a new report that the UAE and Egypt warned Netanyahu, says Netanyahu knew of October 7 in advance and it was 'a stand-down' (Sep 8). Calls Greenland a vital interest under 'hemispheric defense' (Sep 21).

Says the administration is preparing to resume the Iran war after the midterms, with a third carrier and more Marines deploying, while reading the buildup as most likely meant to intimidate Iran (Oct 1); calls the war 'a stalemate… of economic attrition' (Oct 5).

positions.statement: He opposes war with Iran. He says "no war with Iran" was his "rallying cry" in the 2024 election, that Iran poses no strategic threat to the United States, and that a war with Iran would repeat Iraq ("the next worst thing we've ever done"; "the WMD myth"). He says the June 2025 strikes were "not our war" and the 2026 war was launched by Trump "on behalf of Israel": "It's Israel's war."

On Russia itself he has said his view changed. In November 2024 he said "Russia should be an ally of the United States"; in July 2025 he said "I'm no longer as pro-Russia as I used to be"; in December 2025 he said he used to think being pro-Russia was "based and edgy", that he no longer feels that way "based on things that I've seen and things I've learned", and "I don't know that Russia is necessarily going to be an ally," though the US should not "ostracize" it. He discusses Ukraine far less since the Iran war; in March 2026 he cites it, with Iran, as "the true limits of U.S. force projection."

summary: He argues that 'Jewish power', which he also calls 'organized Jewry' or 'world Jewry', is the central problem facing America. He names it alongside 'white genocide' as one of his two core issues and says opposing it is patriotic. He describes it as a transnational network of Jewish organizations and powerful Jews acting as 'a state within a state'. He says this is not about Israel or neocons alone, and that while not every Jew is part of the power structure, Jews organize and 'act as a unit' on the basis of their identity. He claims it put Trump in office and dominates the Republican Party through donors, the lobby and a veto over nominations, directs US military power at Israel's enemies, and runs or 'filters' media, finance and tech, which he calls a 'Jewish oligarchy' creating a 'manufactured reality'. He also ties it to censorship and hate-speech rules, to immigration and diversity, and to Jeffrey Epstein, whom he calls a 'Jewish fixer'. He says the Holocaust death toll was 'probably… far fewer than six million' and calls the Holocaust a 'religious dogma'. His stated remedy is to remove Jews from positions of power, make Israel lobbying illegal, and 'dismantle' groups such as the ADL, SPLC and AIPAC; he says this means taking away power, not rights or lives, and that everyone living in America, 'whether you're a Jew or a Muslim', must put America first or go. He distinguishes his view from what he calls 'low IQ antisemitism' and from blaming Israel for 'literally everything'.

timeline.note: Describes his own project as 'criticism of jewish power' alongside Catholicism, the Israel lobby and 'racialism' (Dec 3). Says the Jewish lobby includes the Israel lobby 'but is also bigger', and that the donors who 'put up the money' are picking Trump's cabinet (Nov 19–22). positions.statement: On the Holocaust, he says he questions "whether the Holocaust happened the way that historians say that it did": "probably it was far fewer than six million", and he doubts "this Hollywood version of exterminating people with gas chambers" (May 2025). He says he does not care how many died because the Holocaust has been "weaponized" against "me and my people" (Dec 2025). He calls the Holocaust 'narrative' a foundation of Jewish power and a 'religious dogma', asks whether Holocaust culture was built by design to give Jews power, calls himself a 'Holocaust revisionist', and praises David Irving. positions.statement: He argues that the National Conservatism Conference (NatCon), founded and run by Yoram Hazony, "this Jewish dual citizen from Israel", is "a pro-Israel Zionist si-op" whose purpose is "to sneak a pro-Israel agenda into the nationalist cause". In his account it was seeded with Peter Thiel's money and gave a platform to Vance, Rubio, Hawley, DeSantis and Tucker Carlson, while banning ethno-nationalists and Israel critics ("He banned Peter Brimelow, he banned me"), so that one can be a nationalist "only in a pro-Israel way, not in a racialist way, not in a pro-white way". He says the project exists to siphon dissident nationalist energy into a Vance or Rubio 2028 campaign, and that the second Trump administration "implemented the policies of NatCon". When the October 2026 conference was held in Jerusalem with Ben Gvir and Smotrich speaking, he called it confirmation of what he had said for years, and described Hazony's 'virtue of nationalism' as a Straussian project whose hidden aim is to win American support for Israel taking the West Bank. He holds that American nationalism "can never be controlled by a dual citizen from Israel" and must instead affirm race and exclude Jews as "Semitic, Eastern, and Jewish".

summary: He presents America First, his groyper movement, as an exclusive, right-wing, Christian and pro-white American nationalism, and as the true heir to Trump's 2016 program. In his account, Trump was only 'a stepping stone' and MAGA has since been captured. His strategy is leverage and long-term entry into institutions rather than street action: an organized bloc that withholds its votes, and disciplined young men moving into Young Republicans, campaigns and government while hiding their 'power level'. He disavows violence and costumed rallies. He says the right has moved toward him and the groypers have won the argument, but that the movement must stay rigorous and keep apart from conspiracy cranks, rival splinters and Thiel-network imitators who copy it without race and Jews. He describes one change of strategy himself: in 2025 he floated issue-by-issue cooperation with the populist left, and in July 2026 he said that coalition with the left and Muslims 'made sense two years ago, but it doesn't anymore'.

timeline.period: Before the transcripts (as he recounts it)
timeline.note: He starts as a pro-Trump student commentator in 2016–17 and says Ben Shapiro first called him an antisemite in Dec 2016. The 'Groyper War' against Turning Point USA follows in fall 2019, then bans and blacklisting. He says that in 2022 he campaigned against Joe Kent 'to impose a cost' for disavowing him.

After the election he calls the Trump movement 'an insufficient first step' and 'in terminal decline' (Nov 21 2024). He calls his movement 'the heirs to the 2016 campaign… It isn't Trump. It isn't Vance' (Jan 23 2025) and says 'the MAGA movement left me' (Mar 3). He describes a Thiel and Silicon Valley effort to de-radicalize young white men through 'colorblind meritocracy' (Nov 2024 – Jan 2025), and urges running far-right spoilers for leverage (Feb 25). He asks to be rehabilitated because 'the right wing has moved closer to me' (Apr 23), and declares 'I'm a Christian nationalist. I'm a white nationalist' (Jun 10).

He says Turning Point's Israel 'struggle session' shows 'we have already prevailed' (Jul 24) and calls Trump 'a stepping stool' (Jul 30). He wants a voting bloc that puts 'the fear of God in these Republicans' (Aug 20) and floats a 'coalition of the willing' (Aug 26). After Charlie Kirk's assassination he disavows any follower who takes up arms and tells young men to build careers instead (Sep 11). He demands rigor over the Kirk conspiracy theories (Sep 17–19).

After the leaked Young Republican chat he reframes 'infiltration' as an 'elite human capital strategy' (Oct 14–15). The Tucker Carlson interview follows: 'We won the argument' (Nov 4); 'you can have the Israel first money or… the America first votes' (Oct 30); MAGA is over, 'only gonna be America first' (Nov 17). He floats left-right populist cooperation over the Epstein petition (Nov 19, Crowder interview Dec 4). He warns of a 'mimic' movement led by Tucker and Vance (Dec 1, Dec 26) and refuses to pledge his 2028 vote (Dec 26).

He says the movement is in an 'antisemitism bubble' manipulated by 'communists… Islamists, third-worldists' and must be explicitly right-wing (Jan 12). He separates himself from 'JQ Anon' (Jan 23) and declares a 'JQ recession' (Feb 26). He urges a Democratic vote in 2026 as leverage (see `midterms`). In May he rejects the rival America First United conference and Dan Bilzerian (May 4–12) and ends his unity approach: 'No more unity' (May 25). He says 'we won' over the Daily Wire but warns against overplaying (May 14), and calls a student's anti-Jewish stunt 'reckless and self-sabotaging' (Jun 17).

He says the coalition with Muslims and the left 'made sense two years ago, but it doesn't anymore' (Jul 6). He rejects Patriot Front-style street activism for an 'officer class' (Jul 6), says Trump must be rejected 'wholesale' (Jul 13), and cites reports that 40–75% of young GOP staffers are groypers (Aug 3). He tells followers to build a Young Republican network for 2027–28 (Aug 18) and calls Tucker's manifesto an effort to 'deflate… white nativist feelings' (Aug 5). He declares 'the Trump movement is dead' (Sep 22). In the Straka interview (Oct 5) he says 'I don't think we need allies' and welcomes anyone who puts America first.

After a Wall Street Journal piece in which Ted Cruz says 'the Groyper problem is real' and that many applicants to his Senate office reject his support for Israel, he calls it vindication of the entryism strategy, says groypers already hold 'very critical positions in the admin', and describes the movement as also a pressure group that 'must be placated' (Oct 14).

positions.statement: He defines America First as an exclusive, right-wing, Christian and 'on some level' pro-white American nationalism: Americans first before Israel and organized Jewry, immigrants, capital and technology. He calls himself 'a Christian nationalist' and 'a white nationalist', presents 'Christ is King' as deliberately exclusionary, and sets the movement against conservatism, 'inclusive populism', 'multi-racial working class populism' and 'colorblind meritocracy'. He says his quarrel with Jews is that an organized, powerful group uses American power for Israel, and that America First is not merely anti-Israel. The exclusivity is of program, not of membership: 'pro-white not to the exclusion of everybody else', and in interviews he says anyone who puts America first is welcome (see movement-07).

positions.statement: He argues that his movement, not Trump or Vance, is the heir to Trump's 2016 America First campaign. His verdict on Trump has been the same throughout: a necessary but insufficient first step, 'a stepping stone', 'phase one' and 'a John the Baptist' toward a true nationalism. In November 2024 he called the Trump movement 'on net very positive' and 'insufficient'; in July 2026 he still called it 'a necessary first step, totally inadequate'. He says MAGA left him rather than the reverse, and that personal loyalty to Trump is misplaced. Because Trump is now 'suffocating rather than nurturing' the next wave, he says in 2026 that the movement must reject Trump 'wholesale' and build what comes after, and that the Trump movement is dead and captured by the system.

positions.statement: He argues the movement wins power through elite institutions, not protest. He calls this an 'elite human capital strategy' and an 'officer class', a generational project after which the groypers 'are just gonna be the GOP'. After a leaked Young Republican chat in Oct 2025 he adds operational caution: disappearing messages and no 'edgelording' in writing. By Oct 2026 he describes the establishment as having conceded the wider culture and retreated to defending its institutions, by refusing to hire or promote groypers, and says the movement is already inside them. In Oct 2026 he lays out the reasoning: every elite sector (the academy, donors, the media) ultimately works through government, so followers must go to Washington, because 'you can't be a plumber and change government'.

positions.statement: He polices who is in and out of the movement. Politicians who disavow him or others over Israel or race must pay a cost: he says he campaigned against Joe Kent in 2022 'to impose a cost', and he tells followers to punish those who disavow Tucker Carlson. He rejects rival 'America First' splinters and late-arriving influencers (the America First United conference, Dan Bilzerian, Jake Shields) as having no ideology beyond hostility to Jews, and in May 2026 ended his 'unity' approach ('No more unity') in favor of a small committed vanguard. Former opponents can come on board on the movement's terms: he told Tucker Carlson in October 2025 that if Marjorie Taylor Greene 'wanted to be aligned… I would totally be on board with her', and told Brandon Straka in October 2026 that the movement does not depend on such figures ('I don't think we need allies'): a candidate will emerge and others must decide whether to back them. Asked by Straka who is welcome, he said 'everybody that wants to put America first', including Jews and gay people, 'as long as they put America first', while arguing that everyone benefits if America's demographics and Christian heritage are preserved.

positions.statement: He argues the movement can only persuade normal people if it is rigorous, evidence-based and credible, and must avoid crankery, 'JQ Anon' conspiracy content and heuristic thinking in which Israel or Jews are blamed for everything. He made this case most sharply against the Charlie Kirk assassination theories (see `right-media`). He warns his side not to 'overplay our hand', says its strength is being 'a vessel for the truth', and calls for 'elite human capital' and researchers rather than grifters. He holds that this is no softening: 'I want the edifice of Jewish control to fall.'

summary: He argues that America is a white, European and Christian country, and that its future as one is the central question of politics. He wants it to stay or again become majority white, and he defines the nation by ancestry and shared blood rather than by creed. He calls on whites to 'take your own side': to develop a racial consciousness and organize as a group, as he says Jews, blacks and other groups already do. He rejects 'colorblind meritocracy' and race-blind, economics-first populism (Ramaswamy, Vance, Tucker Carlson) as deliberate efforts to defuse white identity. He describes an anti-white double standard in law, politics and media, calls himself a 'race realist' who attributes racial disparities to genetics, and opposes race-mixing, which he says disqualifies Vance and others from leading the cause. He says Jews are not white and promote diversity in America while keeping Israel a Jewish state, and he casts South Africa as the prototype of a white minority's fate. From late 2025 he says the left is anti-white 'race communism' and, by 2026, that American politics is 'a race war'. He repeatedly says this should be pursued through organizing and institutional power, not violence.

summary: He argues the Republican Party is run for its donors (Wall Street, business wanting cheap labor, Silicon Valley, and the Israel lobby and Jewish donors) and not its voters, and that it betrays its base on immigration and everything else in a 'promise-and-sell-out' cycle as old as Reagan. He calls conservatism 'controlled opposition', ruled by an upper class that skin-suits every insurgency, and holds that neoconservatism is Jewish at its root and still steers Republican foreign policy. In his account the establishment absorbed Trumpism rather than being overturned by it, the center right gatekeeps the far right more harshly than the left does, the two parties form a uniparty, and the GOP 'refuses to pander' to young white men. He no longer calls himself a Republican. His strategy for the party is one plan: 'burn' its current leadership 'to the ground' (primary them, fire them), then take the GOP over as 'the only viable vehicle' for his movement.

timeline.note: After the election he says the elite 'accepted Trump but not MAGA' and points to the Gaetz withdrawal and the cabinet picks (Waltz, Hegseth, Rubio, 'neocon'). He says donors are already 'pumping the brakes' on deportations (Nov 20), that the GOP has been 'controlled by Israelis for decades' (Feb 4), that conservatism puts 'a speed limit on liberalism' (Jan 28), and that the Trump movement has been 'skin suited by imitators' (Feb 17). Feb 5: the establishment 'is seeking a compromise with the base'.

Mar 3: 'MAGA is now defined by people like Lindsey Graham and Tim Scott and Vivek Ramaswamy.' Mar 11: Republicans 'capitulate and surrender' on spending. Conservative parties are 'controlled opposition' (Feb 25); 'Conservatism is an ideology of convenience for a set of donors' (May 26). He describes neocons against restrainers in the Pentagon and the White House (Apr–Jun), and says AIPAC 'arranges' Jewish billionaire donors for Ted Cruz (Jun 18). Jul 3: he credits Trump's budget bill as a 'landmark historic victory' over establishment delay, then attacks the farm-labor plan as amnesty.

Aug 8: a long segment arguing neoconservatism is Jewish at its core. Aug 19: the GOP 'has never… done anything for me' and 'refuse[s] to pander to us'. Aug 25: no longer aligned with a party 'controlled by Israel… Wall Street… Silicon Valley'. Sep: 'I'm not owned by the GOP.' Sep 23: the Kirk memorial shows the GOP 'does not like its own base'.

The Heritage Foundation episode (Nov 3–7): Kevin Roberts's defense of Tucker Carlson, then donors 'yanking his chain'; he says gatekeeping is the pro-Israel side's 'next line of defense' (Nov 10). Nov 5: 'I'm not a Republican… I almost think about starting my own party.' Nov 10: the shutdown is 'not a real fight'. Feb 2026: 'We want to burn the Republican party to the ground'; the GOP's 'dirty little secret' is donor funding against working-class votes (Feb 18).

Mar 10: conservatism is a base ruled by 'a different class' that subverts it; 'Our enemy is the leadership of our own controlled opposition.' The center right 'works with the far left against the far right' (Apr 28) and is 'the biggest enemy of right-wing nationalism' (May 7). He calls the GOP 'the only viable vehicle' (Jul 8) and says it must be taken over. Jul 13: 'the GOP has conquered the revolution' (after the Graham memorials). Aug 4: under Trump the center right is 'more exclusionary towards the far right than the left was'. Sep 23: Trump became 'the savior of the GOP'; donors get what they want 'every single time'. Sep 29: the Sarah Huckabee Sanders ad shows the GOP 'attacking white men'. Oct 5 (Straka interview): he recalls choosing at 18 to work 'as a pressure group' from outside.

After the Ted Cruz piece he predicts a coordinated purge of groyper staffers, with the left and the establishment right 'working together': the left exaggerates the problem to paint Republicans as extremists, and the establishment uses it to put pressure on people like Tucker and push them out (Oct 14).

passages.title: Who got mugged by reality

They were Jewish leftists that got mugged by reality. In particular, they were Jewish leftists who were backed by the CIA that got mugged by reality. … Well, Irving Kristol and Norman Podhoretz had say in their own words They realized that the left had gone to radical when it turned against Israel When the Soviet Union under Leonid Brezhnev started promulgating an anti-Israel doctrine On the basis that Israel was a colonial capitalist power, when the Soviet Union backed Egypt and Syria to the hilt, so much so they almost defeated Israel. And when the non-Jewish American left turned against Israel and made those same arguments that Israel is racist, Israel is a settler colonial state, Israel is an outpost of capitalism and colonialism. passages.title: The classic construction
passages.text: These are two center right guys that have a job at the blaze, have a job at the Paul Singer funded Manhattan Institute. They've never been censored in their lives. They never got banned on Twitter. They never got banned on YouTube and they still aren't. They never got banned on PayPal. … This is the classic construction. Which is that the center right works with the far left against the far right every single time. The far left wages war on the far right and the center right joins them hand in hand. … The center right for a decade would say, we're against cancel culture, we're against censorship. They never got censored and they never got canceled. They remained gainfully employed and they had all of the platforms available to them. The people that were being canceled and censored were the proud boys, the alt-right. Red Ice, TRS, Richard Spencer, people like myself. Did Ben Shapiro, did the people at CPAC, did the Blaze, did any of them ever stick up for us? No, no, because they were in a handshake agreement with the far left. The far left wants to far right destroyed, and that means that you get this very moderate and weak and flaccid center right that isn't really a threat.
passages.context: Apr 2026, on two center-right commentators who have never been censored

positions.statement: He argues the two parties form a uniparty: 'The Democrats and the Republicans are the same thing.' In his account the establishments of both parties and the permanent bureaucracy have run one foreign policy for 30 years, the 'deep state really wins no matter what', shutdown fights are staged ('This is not a real fight'), and Republicans collude with Democrats to block radical change such as ending the filibuster for the SAVE Act. He refines this in two ways: he says a Republican president was needed to sell the Iran war because the GOP is controlled by the Israel lobby, and that a Democratic House will make the impasses real.

quotes.text: It seems like the deep state really wins no matter what, whether it's Biden or Trump, it's the same policy.
quotes.context: on Biden authorizing long-range strikes into Russia, as Mike Waltz said Trump would

quotes.text: whether you have the center left party and the liberal Jewish network or the center right party and the conservative Zionist international network, you're getting the same stuff.
quotes.context: on right-wing governments taking office while policy on immigration and war stays the same

quotes.text: The Democrats and the Republicans are the same thing. They're exactly the same thing.
quotes.context: arguing the GOP stokes white grievance to win support for Israel aid and corporate tax cuts

quotes.text: a Republican president would be the one that would support this effort, more than the Democrats
quotes.context: arguing that after October 7 a Republican president was chosen to sell the Iran war 'because the GOP is controlled by the Israel lobby'

quotes.text: They're all in the same uni party. the political establishments of both parties, as well as the permanent bureaucracy, which is inside the government.
quotes.context: recollection of his Jul 1 2025 debate with Dinesh D'Souza, who called him a Democrat

quotes.text: this is why I'm so done with Republican, Democrat, vote Republican to defeat the Democrats, because this is just what you get. This is not a real fight.
quotes.context: on the Nov 2025 shutdown ending without concessions, which he calls staged

quotes.text: when you have a Democrat-controlled house, these like symbolic government shutdowns, these become real impasses.
quotes.context: refining his view of shutdowns: kayfabe now, real once Democrats win the House

quotes.text: SAVE Act can't do it. Mass deportations can't do it. All these things that the voters are told politically impossible. … And that's when you realize it is still the uniparty.
quotes.context: Dave Smith interview (Part of the Problem), May 18 2026, contrasting the deportation drawdown 'too unpopular for the midterms' with the Iran war

quotes.text: But Republicans are colluding with Democrats to prevent this from happening.
quotes.context: on why Republicans will not end the filibuster to pass the SAVE Act

passages.title: A cordon sanitaire
passages.text: The Republicans can change the rules and say actually we only need a simple majority. We only need 50 plus one They could do that tomorrow They could do it tomorrow. They could pass the save act. … Why won't they do it? It's because they're not really serious. They don't really want to. You see, because Republicans and Democrats, they maintain this very delicate balance. trading the House and the Senate and the White House every couple of years, trading it back and forth. And there is this consensus that neither side wants to rock the boat too much. There's sort of this cordon sanitaire where they want to keep out the far right, keep out the far left. … They actually are united in the fact that they don't want change. They don't want any meaningful, radical, sweeping, legitimate, significant change from either side. And what they all agree on is the military budget gets bigger. The welfare state grows bigger. The bureaucracy grows bigger. They agree that the oligarchy and their interests are going to be protected. Israel's going to get their foreign aid and their wars and the rest of it. … But Republicans are colluding with Democrats to prevent this from happening. Republicans in the upper chamber, in the Senate, which represents the states, which represents the interests, they are in agreement with the Democrats as a cartel that they will impede radical change. And this is why nothing will ever get better.
passages.context: Jun 2026, on Republicans' refusal to end the filibuster to pass the SAVE Act

positions.statement: On his own relation to the party: he says he is independent of the GOP ('I'm not owned by the GOP'), no longer aligned with a party 'controlled by Israel… Wall Street… Silicon Valley', and in November 2025 said 'I'm not a Republican' (adding, once, that he had almost thought of starting his own party). His plan for the party is to destroy its current leadership and capture it. When he says the GOP 'needs to be burned to the ground', he means its officeholders and this administration: 'We want to primary you. We want to fire you. And then we want to build a different party.' He calls the GOP 'the only viable vehicle left for people like us' and says the aim is 'to take over the GOP as the vehicle of the political opposition'. In August 2025, calling for a realignment, he said he would 'prefer to vote for a young Republican that can deliver'.

quotes.text: I no longer find myself aligned with a party that is controlled by Israel, that is controlled by Wall Street, that is controlled by Silicon Valley, that is cutting corporate taxes.
quotes.context: calling for a political realignment

quotes.text: I would prefer to vote for a Republican. I prefer to vote for a young Republican that can deliver on what Trump promised.
quotes.context: Aug 25 2025, same passage; he says he would also consider a Democrat 'that's not anti-white' (see white-identity)

quotes.context: contrasting himself with influencers seeking White House access

quotes.context: after Republican losses in Virginia and New Jersey and Kevin Roberts's apology; he continues 'and so expensive'

quotes.text: We want to burn the Republican party to the ground.
quotes.context: Feb 5 2026, rebutting the charge that he wants to 'rule the ashes'; he names 'this administration' and the officeholders who 'made false promises', and continues 'We want to primary you. We want to fire you. And then we want to build a different party'

quotes.context: arguing the GOP must be destroyed so it can be captured

quotes.context: explaining why losing 2026 to Democrats could 'reset' the party, though 'nothing good for whites' comes from Democratic rule

quotes.context: Professor Jiang debate, Sep 26 2026, on baby boomers as the base of the Republican Party

passages.title: A hostile takeover
passages.text: So if you recognize the Republican party is the vehicle of opposition, it is the opposition party. It is the antithesis of the Democrats. And what does it mean as, as a vehicle? It means they have institutions. The Republican party is on the ballot everywhere. They've got the infrastructure. They've got the personnel. It is an all in one package. … You're gonna get everything for Israel, nothing for us. The people that are running the party, the people that are in the party, they are operatives of foreign governments, foreign intelligence, billionaires. You're gonna get big agriculture. You're gonna get the Israel lobby. You're gonna get Wall Street, little tech, chamber of commerce. So the Republican party is not really an option in its current form. … And so what you have to realize is the only way for us to achieve power is to take over the GOP as the vehicle of the political opposition and make it reflect the real opposition. But the only way this can be done is if they are weakened, if they are sufficiently weakened, then they can be captured. If there's fewer of them, if they have less money, we need to look at them as like a depreciating asset. We are like private equity. We need to come in, we need the Republican party. We need their stock price to go really, really low so that we can have a hostile takeover. That's how you have to look at it.
passages.context: May 2026, on the GOP as the only vehicle of opposition; the private-equity analogy is about elections

positions.statement: He argues the GOP does not care about white people, above all young white men. It panders to every other group ('They will pander to black people… to Jews, to Zionists. They refuse to pander to us'). In his account it has 'never… done anything for me', treats him as 'just another expendable young white man', 'threw me away when I was 18', and now attacks white men outright, as in Sarah Huckabee Sanders's September 2026 welfare ad, while defending Indians and courting new minorities. He reads the party's 'broaden the coalition' outreach as 'the euphemism for the white man is dying out'.

quotes.text: The Republican Party has never, ever, in my entire life, done anything for me. To make my life better, to make my life easier, never, never.
quotes.context: listing housing, jobs, H-1B visas, wars and feminism

quotes.text: They will pander to black people. They will pander to women. They will pander to Hispanics. They will pander to billionaires, to Jews, to Zionists. They refuse to pander to us.
quotes.context: on why his vote is a bargaining chip

quotes.context: refusing to rally to the GOP after Charlie Kirk's memorial

quotes.context: same passage

quotes.text: I am just another expendable young white man that they don't give a fuck about.
quotes.context: explaining why he is done with Republicans

quotes.text: The GOP is attacking white men, what else is new? That's what they've always done.
quotes.context: on Sarah Huckabee Sanders's welfare-to-work ad depicting a young white man as the abuser

quotes.text: This is the euphemism for the white man is dying out. So forget them. We now need to pivot and pander to all these new minorities.
quotes.context: same segment, contrasting the GOP's defense of Indians after the Texas football-game controversy
