summary: He sees most of right-wing media as a paid influencer class and an Israel-aligned gatekeeping apparatus. Its center is Ben Shapiro and the Daily Wire, which he says blacklisted him in 2016 and whose decline he treats as a groyper victory, along with Mark Levin, Laura Loomer and Josh Hammer, whom he calls foreign agents for Israel. He was a long-time adversary of Charlie Kirk and Turning Point USA, but after Kirk's assassination he called him a martyr and rejected the theories that Israel killed him, arguing they discredit the Israel-critical right. That set him against Candace Owens, whose arc runs from a welcomed but 'survivalist' latecomer to a 'grifter'. He treats the newer Israel-critical voices (Owens, Ian Carroll, Dave Smith, Megyn Kelly) as latecomers and a possible limited hangout. Among streamers, he defends Andrew Tate against what he calls political prosecutions and turned on Sneako in 2026. Tucker Carlson has his own topic (`tucker`).

timeline.period: Before the transcripts (as he recounts it)
timeline.note: He says Ben Shapiro called him an antisemite and the Daily Wire circle cut him off in Dec 2016, when he was 18. He led the fall 2019 'Groyper War' against Charlie Kirk and Turning Point USA, then was banned from their events.

He says influencers have benefactors and he is 'the only one that isn't owned' (Feb 25) and that they are 'paid to post a script' (Jun 2). He welcomes Candace Owens, Ian Carroll and Andrew Tate going mainstream on Israel but calls Owens and Sneako 'survivalists' and asks for credit (Feb 7, Mar 6). He calls the Daily Wire an Israel-first company and launches a campaign for Walsh and Knowles to quit (Mar 4–25). He calls Tate's prosecution political persecution (Mar 28), Dave Smith 'promoted' opposition (May 12), and Levin, Shapiro and Loomer 'undeclared foreign agents' (Jun 23).

He says Kirk is 'being paid by Israel' over Gaza (Jul 28) and suggests a Russian angle in Owens's Macron series (Jul 24). Carlson and Owens attack him on Carlson's show, and he answers with a three-hour rebuttal (Aug 1). He asks whether Carlson, Kelly, Kirk and Owens are a 'limited hangout' and calls himself 'the litmus test' (Aug 22).

Kirk is assassinated (Sep 10): 'I consider him a true martyr' (Sep 11). He rejects the Israel-did-it theory (Sep 15–19) and says the Netanyahu letter shows Kirk 'supported Israel until the day that he died' (Sep 29). He calls Levin, Hammer and Loomer 'foreign agents' who should be deported (Sep 29) and the trio 'Groyper MVPs' (Nov 7). He says Shapiro wants Carlson, Owens and him blacklisted (Nov 7). He defends Sneako (Oct 8, Nov 10). His feud with Owens over her Kirk series escalates around Turning Point's Dec 15 stream: 'Candice is a grifter' (Dec 10).

He defends the Tates over the Miami club incident (Jan 20–21). He says Owens, Carroll and Carlson push every conspiracy 'except… the Jews themselves' (Jan 23) and that Owens and Carlson are 'not pro-white' (Jan 26). He praises Walsh's defense of Erika Kirk (Feb 26). During the Iran war he says Trump called Loomer first (Mar 17), is 'owned by Mark Levin' (Apr 1), and that late converts 'have no credibility' (Apr 8). He treats the Daily Wire's layoffs and collapse as a win (May 1, May 14, Jun 23). He breaks with Sneako (May 25) and calls him 'a civilizational enemy' (Jun 9).

After Tyler Robinson's preliminary hearing he says he was vindicated, that people owe Erika Kirk an apology, and that the Kirk conspiracy is 'a major blow' to alternative media (Jul 9–10). He calls the Tates' Miami arrest political (Jul 20). He scores the Owens–Andrew Wilson debate a loss for Owens on evidence (Aug 17). He declines to attack Owens's private life but calls her work a grift (Sep 28). In the Straka interview he calls Turning Point an empty coalition and says Owens and Carlson are 'giving Ben Shapiro a lifeline' (Oct 5).

positions.statement: He argues that most of the right-wing influencer class is bought: commentators are paid by donors, PACs, the party, Silicon Valley (the Thiel / 'PayPal mafia' network) or foreign governments to post scripted lines, so they relay power's message to the base rather than the base's demands to power. He calls news media 'effectively a form of… political lobbying' that need not turn a profit because billionaires keep its pro-Israel outlets afloat. He says he is attacked and blacklisted because he is 'the only one that isn't owned', and that the gatekeepers lost their ten-year effort to suppress him.

quotes.text: The reason that everyone hates me, a big reason, the reason that everyone lies about me is because I'm the only one that isn't owned.
quotes.context: on influencers piling on Ashley St. Clair to please Musk; he says others have benefactors in Israel, the Trump campaign or the Gulf

quotes.text: Do you know that every conservative influencer that you follow is paid to post a script?
quotes.context: on Palantir coverage and a platform paying conservative influencers per scripted post

quotes.text: These Republican influencers, they get a script from one of these groups, a consultancy from the party itself, wherever, and then they get paid by the post to put out the script.
quotes.context: after a dozen influencers posted the same line about Trump's signature on the Epstein birthday letter

quotes.text: For 10 years, they tried to censor me, blacklist me in order to squelch and suppress my ideas, and they objectively lost that battle.
quotes.context: on Shapiro, Levin and Hammer doing damage control after his Tucker Carlson interview

quotes.text: now they just pay influencers. This is a real thing. This is not metaphor. This is how it works, logistically.
quotes.context: after pro-Trump influencers all pushed the White House ballroom following the Correspondents' Dinner shooting

quotes.text: it feels like these other influencers, like you say, like a Benny Johnson, a Steven Crowder, et cetera, they're facing us with their back to the party. And everything the administration does, their job is to sell it to us so that we are prepared to go out and vote in the midterms, vote in the next cycle, whatever. And so it does just become like, you are a regime apologist.…it's sort of like your job is to launder this to us
quotes.context: interview with Dave Smith, May 2026, on pro-Trump influencers such as Benny Johnson and Steven Crowder

quotes.text: The purpose of news media is, it's effectively a form of lobbying. It's effectively a form of political lobbying.
quotes.context: on why the Daily Wire does not need to be profitable

passages.title: Now they just pay influencers
passages.text: Politicians and corporations and foreign governments would engage lobbyists. They would pay specialists lots of money, and this is heavily regulated by the government. There are disclosures and there are rules and there are monetary limits and all kinds of things. Those lobbyists would use their connections in media, in government, among the political movers and shakers and they would try to accomplish the goals of those political parties, corporations … and foreign governments. And now foreign governments, corporations, and political parties and entities, now they just pay influencers. This is a real thing. This is not metaphor. This is how it works, logistically. They pay influencers. They pay them hundreds, sometimes thousands of dollars, sometimes more than that. It's completely unregulated. It's totally under the table. And it literally works like that. They say, we will pay you $3,000. If you post a TikTok and here's the script and the script has to say this, this and this, they tell the influencers, make it your own. Say it in your own words, but we need this hashtag and these are the points to emphasize and these are the things that you have to say.
passages.context: Apr 2026, on right-wing influencers posting the same talking points at the same time

positions.statement: He casts Ben Shapiro as an 'Israel first Jew', 'not a conservative… not an American patriot', and the Daily Wire as an Israel-first 'Jewish supremacist' company that fired Candace Owens and is kept alive by billionaire money. His feud is personal and dated: he says Shapiro called him an antisemite and had him blacklisted at 18, in Dec 2016, for noting that the Daily Wire never criticized Israel, and has refused to debate him for years. He says Shapiro wants Carlson, Owens and him blacklisted, and treats the Daily Wire's 2025–26 decline and layoffs as proof that people are 'sick of the pro-Israel spin' and that Shapiro was exposed as more loyal to Israel than to America.

quotes.text: If he gets exposed and then ultimately defeated on the basis that he is more loyal to Israel than America, the day that happens, this is a new right wing.
quotes.context: on reports of the Daily Wire's financial trouble: Shapiro 'was supposed to be the next generation… pro-Israel conservative'

quotes.text: I try to get Ben Shapiro in a debate for seven years. People have offered money.
quotes.context: on Daily Wire hosts saying they will debate anyone but not him

quotes.text: I tweeted at Ben Shapiro. I said, you know, I've never seen anything on the daily wire that's actually critical of Israel.
quotes.context: recollection: telling Carlson how his break with Shapiro began in Dec 2016, when he was 18

quotes.text: That is why Shapiro canceled me on Christmas. In 2016, because I, before I said anything, I said, you have never criticized Israel.
quotes.context: recollection, answering Shapiro's 40-minute video of his clips: the blacklisting predates them

quotes.context: on Shapiro's Megyn Kelly interview, which he says pressed Kelly, Vance and Turning Point to cut off Carlson, Owens and him

quotes.text: I think it is the media environment in general, which is to say that people are sick of the pro-Israel spin.
quotes.context: on the Daily Wire layoffs; he notes the top podcasts are now Israel-critical

quotes.context: on the New Yorker piece about the Daily Wire's decline

quotes.context: on reports that the Daily Wire is seeking a $100 million bailout despite falling numbers

passages.title: Why Shapiro's fall matters
passages.text: Shapiro was supposed to be the vanguard for all of the pro-Israel conservatives. If people like Bill Kristol self-immolated being never Trumpers, if they're out of touch, if they called it wrong, you know, they kind of bet their chips on like a socially liberal, environmentally friendly, super liberal generation, CGOP. Then what Shapiro was supposed to be was the next saga. He was supposed to be the next generation, an internet savvy, cool, memeable, owning the Libs, Jewish pro-Israel conservative. So if he goes down, that means that project is failed. That means it's over. If he gets exposed and then ultimately defeated on the basis that he is more loyal to Israel than America, the day that happens, this is a new right wing. The day that happens, you have a out and out explicit overt open civil war in the right wing between the Israel critical segment, a pro-Trump populist nationalist, Christian nationalist Israel critical wing, which is embodied by the Gropers, okay, by Nick Fuentes.
passages.context: Mar 2025, on Shapiro as the next-generation pro-Israel conservative after Bill Kristol

passages.title: They lost the youth
passages.text: What ultimately did them in in the end is they no longer had that fuel. They no longer had the subscriber base. They don't have the energy because they lost the youth. It was the youth that fell out of love with Shapiro. When you go and talk to high schoolers and college students and people that have recently graduated college, none of them love Shapiro. Why is that? Despite all those advantages and the head start, they lost their number one secret ingredient because they did not have the truth on their side. They did not have the truth. … And they could censor and they could avoid. They could dodge the debate with me. They could do their little whisper campaign behind the scenes and blacklist all their competition. But over time, it became very transparent that what Shapiro is, is an Israel first Jew. Not a conservative, not a constitutionalist, not a Republican, not an American patriot. Over time, there's nowhere to run. There's nowhere to hide. It became obvious that who is he out for? He's out for Israel.
passages.context: May 2026, on the Daily Wire's decline

positions.statement: He was a long-time adversary of Charlie Kirk and Turning Point USA. He recounts leading the 2019 'Groyper War' against them, and calls Kirk a spokesman for pro-Israel billionaire donors who refused to debate him. In July 2025 he said Kirk was 'being paid by Israel'. After Kirk's assassination he called him 'a true martyr', calling himself 'an adversary, a foe'. He says Kirk remained a loyal defender of Israel until his death, citing the letter to Netanyahu, and was caught between pro-Israel donors and an Israel-critical youth base. He criticized Erika Kirk's memorial and takeover of the organization as a matter of taste ('in poor taste', 'a little premature'), and in Jul 2026, restating that criticism, said people who accused her over the killing owe her an apology. He calls Turning Point an ideologically empty coalition that 'has blown up' without Kirk, and urges groypers to copy its campus-organizing model.

quotes.text: You had these young kids with MAGA hats, Rosaries, crucifixes in line to ask Charlie Kirk, why are you not really a conservative? And it really harmed his reputation and the reputation of his organization.
quotes.context: recollection of the fall 2019 'Groyper War' questioning at Turning Point events

quotes.context: after Kirk said on his show there was no forced starvation in Gaza

quotes.text: And for that, I consider him a true martyr.
quotes.context: special stream the day after the assassination; earlier he calls himself 'an adversary, a foe' of Kirk

I'm out here trying to feel these questions and defend Israel. You gotta help me.…he was basically sandwiched between the donors that needed him to be pro-Israel and his actual base of supporters who needed him not to be.
quotes.context: interview with Brandon Straka, Oct 2026; his paraphrase of the letter, not Kirk's words

positions.statement: His view of Candace Owens changed from qualified welcome to open hostility. In early 2025 he credits her reach and intelligence but calls her a 'survivalist' who spoke on Israel only once it was safe and will not acknowledge the groypers who 'paved the way'. He attacks her Weinstein series and her Macron claims, suggesting a Russian angle. In Aug 2025 he answers her joint attack with Tucker Carlson, which called him a fed and a 'weird kid' in a basement. From Sep 2025 he calls her Kirk-assassination investigation a 'grift' that profits from Kirk's death, calls her attacks on Erika Kirk 'appalling', and questions her husband's family, her donors and her foreign ties. In 2026 he says she is 'not pro-white'. He credits her when he thinks it is due ('if she brings down the daily wire, then she's a patriot'), and in Sep 2026 declined to discuss allegations about her private life ('that's just not something I do').

quotes.text: I think she's very smart. I'm not trying to knock her.…I think that she's a survivalist.

quotes.context: on Carlson and Owens

passages.title: A survivalist
passages.text: You know, Candace Owens kind of waited for all of the smoke to clear and then she jumped in. She wasn't saying that six years ago when it was actually unpopular, but she comes riding in when everyone's been saying it, especially after, so Yay said it in 22. When Israel started killing Palestinians again in 2023, every fucking person was saying it. And then after she comes back from maternity leave and everybody's thoroughly on the Israel hate train, then she comes in like she's, you know, making this big sacrifice. It's like everybody supports this right now. … It's like, okay, but you only really did it when the smoke cleared, when it became popular. … I'm not trying to just dump on all these people. Like I like Candace. I think it's good what she did. … And there's a reason Candace Owens is getting 2 million views per video on YouTube. She's remarkably successful. and she's good at what she does. She knows the timing. She knows how to say it. She knows how to play it. So I think she's very smart. I'm not trying to knock her. I think she's very intelligent. She's very smart. She's very good at it. And there's something to be said about survivalists, but I also think it's important to like know who we're dealing with. I think that she's a survivalist.

positions.statement: He rejects the theories that Israel (or others, including Erika Kirk) killed Charlie Kirk. He says there is no evidence, that Kirk was 'pro-Israel until the day that he died', and that the case against Tyler Robinson is compelling. In Oct 2025 he said the leaked Kirk texts established 'a very clear motive' but that he did not think the killing 'likely'. He argues the theories, pushed by Candace Owens, Max Blumenthal, Ian Carroll and later Tucker Carlson, make Israel critics 'look like idiots', squandered a mandate against left-wing violence and let the left off the hook. He calls them 'a major blow to the credibility' of alternative media, and says Owens lost her Aug 2026 debate with Andrew Wilson by admitting she had no evidence.

positions.statement: He treats the newer Israel-critical voices (Candace Owens, Ian Carroll, Dave Smith, Megyn Kelly, Tim Pool, and Tucker Carlson, who has his own topic) as latecomers and a possible 'limited hangout'. In his account they concede selected points to co-opt the awakened masses, push every conspiracy 'except… the Jews themselves', and are promoted by the establishment as the acceptable opposition. summary: He argues that he is the most censored figure in American politics, and that censorship in America (by platforms, banks, advocacy groups and now the federal government) exists chiefly to suppress talk about race and about Jewish power and Israel, while shielding a licensed conservative establishment. He credits Elon Musk's Twitter and looser platforms for a mass awakening in 2023–25, but says the pro-Israel side is taking control back through the TikTok sale, the Ellison media purchases and renewed ADL pressure, and that the Trump administration has turned state power against Israel's critics. He casts Silicon Valley's 'little tech' as the faction that bought Trump, Palantir as a CIA–Israel surveillance apparatus, and AI as a speculative bubble. He opposes hate-speech laws and government punishment of speech, and argues that turning the left's own tools (firings, prosecutions) back on the left makes 'an even playing field'.

Opposes the AI-regulation moratorium in the One Big Beautiful Bill (Jul 2). Launches America First Plus after banking bans (Jul 28). Answers Musk's fed charge with his list of bans (Aug 11). Musk's purchase showed 'change was possible' (Aug 15). Criticizing Israel 'effectively criminalized' (Aug 21); 'Anti-Semitic speech… should be lawfully protected' (Aug 22). 'Censorship actually got worse since Trump got elected' (Jun 3). Ellison media; Daily Wire bailout (Jun 11–23). 'Larry Ellison acquiring TikTok, that's a Jewish conspiracy all day' (Jul 9). 'The ADL is back' (Jul 10). AI growth 'is speculation and debt' (Jul 14). MAGA bought 'like private equity' (Jul 20). Trump 'is not going to go after big tech' (Jul 29).

Keith Woods refused a US visa: 'Jewish fascism under Trump' and AI-run visa screening (Aug 4). Tech oligarchs' inauguration money was a bribe to run out the clock (Sep 21). positions.statement: He says he has been the most censored and deplatformed person in American politics for a decade, and that it began over Israel: he was blacklisted at 18 after Ben Shapiro called him an antisemite and Cassie Dillon got him banned from CPAC. He lists bans from YouTube (February 2020), Instagram, Facebook and TikTok; from Chase, Bank of America and other banks, PayPal, Stripe and credit-card processing; and from Airbnb, along with the no-fly list and frozen funds under Biden. He attributes the debanking to 'reputational risk' rules that run up to Visa, Mastercard and the Federal Reserve. He cites the bans as proof that he is not a fed or 'propped up'. In 2026 he says the left is still trying to debank him (his super chat processor was shut down in May 2026), and that he is still barred from YouTube, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok and from a check mark on X.

positions.statement: He argues that the platform censorship of roughly 2017–22 targeted two subjects above all: race ('white genocide and white replacement') and 'any criticism of organized Jewry' and Israel. He calls the ADL 'the preeminent Jewish organization' behind censorship and career destruction. In his account it works, with the SPLC and Media Matters, through advertiser boycotts and what he calls a 'reputational protection racket' on advertisers. He says the same system protected the gatekept conservative right: Ben Shapiro, Charlie Kirk and Daily Wire raised money 'fighting censorship' while never being subject to it, so that 'Silicon Valley gives out a license for who gets to have a right-wing opinion.'

passages.title: It was protecting the mainstream right
passages.text: And in that 10 year period, from roughly 2016 until now, or I should say maybe it's a five or six year period from 2017 to 2021, 2022, in that period of the most intense censorship, conservatives were always complaining about censorship. Well, they themselves were never censored. People like Ben Shapiro at Daily Wire and Charlie Kirk at Turning Point USA would fundraise tens of millions of dollars fighting censorship and yet the entire time they were never subject to it. … And this betrays the real purpose of censorship, … Even though the right wing complained about it, even though it was ostensibly coming from the left, it was protecting the mainstream right. It was buttressing the mainstream right because anybody that was further to the right than Charlie Kirk and Ben Shapiro was put out of business. That is good for Ben Shapiro and Charlie Kirk.

passages.title: A reputational protection racket
passages.text: Well, which companies are big enough to have giant advertising budgets in their discretionary budgets to give to media companies? It's the biggest companies. It's the biggest Fortune 500 companies. summary: He presents himself as a Catholic and Christian nationalist. He argues that America is a Christian nation that should be governed by Christians, with Christianity as its state religion though 'not a theocracy', and that 'Christ is King' is meant to be exclusionary. He holds a Catholic supersessionist view of Judaism as defined by the rejection of Christ, calls 'Judeo-Christian' incoherent, and frames history as Christendom ('Rome') against the Jews. He rejects Khazarian, Frankist and occult theories because, he says, they exonerate Jews and Judaism. He opposes Christian Zionism and says Christians must oppose Israel's conduct in Gaza. He calls the Catholic Church the true church and the answer to modernity, urges obedience to the pope, and argues that the country's crisis is spiritual apostasy rather than economics. He treats Catholic sexual morality (against IVF, divorce, contraception and porn; for patriarchy) as a political standard he says both parties have abandoned. He sets Christendom against both Judaism and Islam ('I regard Jews and Muslims as basically the same', 2025), while ranking Islam below Jewish power as a threat to America; in mid-2026 he ended what he calls a 'marriage of convenience' with Muslim critics of Israel.

summary: He treats the succession after Trump as the decisive fight, calling 2028 'the real battle' and saying the ultimate question has always been who fills Trump's shoes. He argues the donors and Peter Thiel's network are trying to crown JD Vance early, while organized pro-Israel money lines up behind Marco Rubio, and he rejects both: from March 2026 he says that if Vance or Rubio is on the ticket he will vote Democrat, and that everyone in the administration is disqualified by the Iran war. His strategy, stated many times: a Democratic Congress from 2026 to 2028 weakens the current GOP and the administration so that anyone from it is too toxic to be viable in 2028, opening space for an outsider from beyond the GOP and administration apparatus. He wants Democrats to win Congress in 2026, not the White House in 2028. He wants that outsider to be an insurgent, radical nationalist who repeats Trump's 2016 hostile takeover of the primary, and casts his own followers as a veto bloc. He calls himself the movement's 'ideological vanguard' rather than its candidate, while not ruling out running for office someday. He expects that if an administration figure is the nominee, Trump's record hands Democrats the White House in 2028.

timeline.note: From the transition on he says the fight is over who succeeds Trump in 2028 and 2032, and that 'it cannot be Vance' (Jan 23 2025). He predicts the GOP will push Vance in 2028 (Nov 21 2024), says 2028 offers 'an opportunity for genuine radicalism' (Jan 20 2025), jokes he is 'all in' for Ye in 2028 (Feb 7), and says he won't vote for Vance in 2028 (Apr 22).

Burning his MAGA hat over the amnesty talk and the Epstein memo, he says the radical right is withholding its votes: 'Forget the midterms. Forget 28… Fuck Vance' (Jul 8). From August he frames the succession as 'the ultimate battle'. He reads Trump's Aug 5 remarks as anointing Vance and Rubio, 'two of the most vociferous never Trumpers'. He threatens to campaign against Vance in Iowa if Vance is the nominee (Aug 19). In October he worries Democrats will 'come back with a vengeance' in 2028 and says the right 'might need a Republican to win', just not Vance (Oct 9). Oct 28: 'in 2028, I'm an undecided voter.'

Nov 11: 'The real battle is 2028'; he tells young followers to be in Iowa and New Hampshire by 2027. He warns Vance that groypers will follow him through the early primary states, and that Shapiro and Levin will 'anoint' Rubio (Nov 4). He refuses to pledge his 2028 vote until he sees the candidates (Dec 26). After Vance condemns him: 'I don't care if you're the nominee… You are not getting my vote' (Feb 5). He floats an America First spoiler strategy (Feb 11) and calls for 'a Caesar' (Feb 12).

Mar 2: the Iran war is 'disqualifying'; if Vance or Rubio is on the 2028 ticket 'I'm voting for a Democrat'. Mar 5: everyone in the administration is disqualified. He calls 2028 'the last dance'. He frames the Iran war as a Vance–Rubio proxy fight and says Rubio escapes the blame. May 6–7: he wants Democrats to win in 2026 but not in 2028, and calls for an open, crowded primary in which a nationalist could win on a plurality.

He says Trump's half-measures are 'charging up' a left-wing populist pendulum that will be 'brutal' in 2028 (Jun 23), and, saying 'I don't want this to happen', that Trump's damage to the brand may mean suffering a Democratic term 'to have a true reset' (Jul 13). He rules himself out as the candidate ('It's not gonna be me', Jun 25) and asks for a 'brilliant handsome white man'. Sep: he hopes Vance is the nominee and 'gets annihilated', predicts Democrats will prosecute Trump officials after winning in 2028, and builds 'a war chest… against JD Vance'. In the Oct 5 Straka interview he lays out the strategy in full (a heavy midterm defeat 'weakens everybody in this administration' and 'opens up a space for someone outside'), predicts a Vance–Rubio race and a likely Democratic win if it comes to that, calls his faction a veto bloc, names Bannon as someone he'd like to see run, calls himself 'the ideological vanguard', and says running for office is 'not off the table'.

summary: He treats feminism as one of the three forces "killing our country", with mass migration and what he calls "our Jewish oligarchy", and argues it must be "eradicated". In his account women's role is secondary and domestic, politics is "the domain of men", and women hold power without accountability, which he says the 2026 Lindsay Clancy and Cornell cases prove. He casts the mainstream right, from 'wife guys' to conservative women commentators, as feminist, is skeptical of 'Me Too' accusations, and opposes transgenderism, the acceptance of homosexuality among the right's leaders, pornography and surrogacy (his Catholic doctrine on sex and marriage is under christianity).

timeline.note: The 'wifejak' fight: he calls the wife-guy trend 'a soft form of male feminism', says 'we need to dismantle feminism completely' and 'politics is domain of men', and calls pronatal content astroturf by tech donors. On the first trans member of Congress: 'ban them from public life'. Says voting Trump brought 'gays and Jews in the cabinet'.

Praises Trump's anti-trans orders as 'righteous' but 'a speed limit on liberalism'; 'there is no such thing as transgender people'. Opposes the IVF order (see christianity). Defends Andrew Tate: women's role is 'secondary', 'the Me Too era is over', the fertility crisis comes from women's emancipation. Feud with Catholic apologist Trent Horn over women and marriage.

On the Tate–Walsh marriage debate: 'feminism must be eradicated', 'I'm done with trad', 'How about patriarchy?'. After the Minneapolis church shooting: not a transgender story but 'pure evil'; conservatives should 'just stop'.

Tucker Carlson interview on patriarchy and pornography (Oct 27). 'Radically against feminism'. Calls Dave Rubin's surrogacy 'among the most evil things'. Marjorie Taylor Greene's resignation: no women in politics; 'You scratch any Republican woman, you get a feminist'. Candace Owens as proof women are 'never accountable'. Year-end: mass migration, feminism and 'Jewish oligarchy' are killing the country.

The Clavicular clip: hypergamy is 'a law of the land' (Feb). Attacks Trump's SAVE Act post on child transition (Mar). Disavows OnlyFans: 'pornography is evil' (Jun). Graham Platner allegation 'another Me Too fake'; the Tate prosecution is political (Jul). Links Charlie Kirk's killer to a radical-left trans subculture (Jul).

His densest run on the theme. The Lindsay Clancy case: women are 'never liable'; women are 'the number one political enemy' ('I was kidding… but it is also totally true'). The Clavicular charges are 'pedophile hysteria'. The Cornell case (Sep 29–Oct 8) is a hoax: 'Feminism must be eradicated', women 'got to go home', 'female entryism has to be rejected', 'No e-girls'; he breaks with Kim Iverson and Faith Merrill as 'crypto feminists'.

positions.statement: He argues that feminism must be "eradicated", not reformed. He names it with mass migration and "our Jewish oligarchy" as one of the three things "killing our country", and in late 2024 said tech donors had "stripped away the most potent critiques of feminism" from the right. During the Cornell case in October 2026 he says repeatedly that "Feminism must be eradicated from the face of the earth. Otherwise, your civilization is destroyed", tying it to the fertility crisis and to men's role; he adds that this "doesn't mean women" ("we love women Not feminism").

He argues from biology that a woman's "sexual function" means she should not be in the military and perhaps not in the workforce or college, that women "should not have the freedom to wear whatever they want", and in October 2026 that women "cannot have the same rights", "shouldn't even be educated" or have "the same opportunities in the workforce". Of taking away women's rights he has said "it's also not a joke at all". He says this comes from respect and that he is "not in favor of cruelty towards women". His Catholic statements on a wife's subordination are under christianity (ch-07).

positions.statement: He argues that "politics is domain of men" and that women should be kept out of political power. He says his side is "against women having the right to vote" (Nov 2024, adding "we make jokes about them and we're serious about them"), that women should never be president or governor, and that politics is "an extension of war" and therefore "not the domain of women", while saying "I'm not saying this because I hate women". He uses Marjorie Taylor Greene's resignation and Candace Owens as examples ("This is why you can't have women in politics"), lists women with diversity and tolerance as "the three things that bring ruin to a nation", and says "if we are going to repair society it starts with women not having as much power as they have". He calls women "the number one political enemy", a line he says he meant as a joke but is "also totally true". In October 2026 he tells women to "go home" and to "support the men", saying "this is not anti-woman".

positions.statement: He is skeptical of sexual-assault accusations against men and calls the cases he covers "Me Too" fakes or "pedophile hysteria". He said "the Me Too era is over" over a lawsuit against Andrew Tate (Mar 2025). He called the allegation against Senate candidate Graham Platner "another Me Too fake allegation", saying he does not see how sex becomes rape "unless there's like a threat of murder involved, a real threat of violence". He called the Tates' prosecution political ("If you become a political target, you're accused of rape") while saying he condemns what they did. He called the charges against the streamer Clavicular over a 16- or 17-year-old "pedophile hysteria". He calls the Cornell case a left-wing hoax like George Floyd and Covid: the seven men are "disgusting, but they're not rapists", and the accuser should be imprisoned for false accusation.

positions.statement: He holds that "there is no such thing as transgender people" and that people become transgender "because they're mentally ill". In Nov 2024 he said trans people should be banned "from public life", hedging that there are "no easy answers". He praised Trump's anti-trans orders (the ban on surgery for minors is "truly righteous and just") but called them "a speed limit on liberalism", and in March 2026 attacked Trump's SAVE Act post for accepting child surgery with parental consent ("Transgenderism should not exist in America"). He ranks the issue far below race: "I don't care about that at all… do care about the fact that I'm being racially and ethnically replaced". After the Aug 2025 Minneapolis church shooting he said nothing in transgender ideology says "kill children" and told conservatives blaming trans people, Democrats and the media to "just stop". In 2026, discussing Charlie Kirk's killer, he describes violence from a radical-left "tranny subculture" on Discord and lists that shooting among its cases.

positions.statement: He objects to the acceptance of homosexuality and surrogacy among the right's leaders. He warned that voting Trump meant "gays and Jews in the cabinet" (Scott Bessent), says the administration is "filled with gay people, openly gay people" and "very socially liberal", and says Trump and Musk "do not take a strong moral stance against it". He calls surrogacy "among the most evil things short of, let's say, murder" because it deprives a child of its mother, and turns it against Ben Shapiro through Shapiro's friendship with Dave Rubin. Asked by Brandon Straka in October 2026, he said homosexuality should not be "outlawed" but should not "be promoted"; that interview's lines on gay marriage and surrogacy are under christianity (ch-07).

positions.statement: He ties falling birth rates to women's emancipation: "this fertility crisis… has almost everything to do with the role of women, that they're educated". Women should have children young (he cites "mutational load"), and most women's roles "should be conducive towards family formation". He calls the Musk-era "have kids, have babies" content astroturf meant to de-radicalize the right. Having children is no substitute for politics: "Saving America is a real responsibility", and demographic replacement is not solved by his viewers having kids ("It's a political problem"). In September 2026 he says "the government has effectively criminalized sex" and links it to low fertility.
